Verified against the primary law text and DLA Piper (updated Feb 2025): Madagascar's Law No. 2014-038 (2015, Art. 20) restricts cross-border transfer of personal data unless the recipient country offers adequate protection, consent is given, or CMIL authorises it — this is an adequacy-based transfer restriction, not an explicit mandate to store data within Madagascar's borders, and no sectoral (financial/telecoms) data-residency requirement was found. DLA Piper (2025) also notes the law remains not fully effective in practice as no implementing decree has been published, though the CMIL regulator was finally established in Dec 2023. Value Code 1 (no data localisation requirements) is a reasonable fit under the strict 'stored within national borders' definition and is retained, but flagged for human review: BFT/industry commentary (2023) treats this type of adequacy-based transfer restriction as a form of de facto localisation, so a case could be made for Code 3 (sectoral/partial) under a broader reading — a genuinely ambiguous classification call.
